blurb: Massive-headed Canary Islands catch dog, once used for guarding and herding cattle
description: The Presa Canario is a large, muscular mastiff-type dog from Spain's Canary Islands, bred for guarding and herding cattle, with a broad, square head.
answer: The Presa Canario is a large Spanish dog of mastiff or catch-dog type from the Canary Islands, found mostly on Gran Canaria and Tenerife. It stands roughly 56–65 cm and weighs about 40–65 kg, and was traditionally kept as a guard dog and for herding sheep and cattle.

body: The breed descends from the Bardino Majorero, an old dog of the Canary Islands, crossed during the colonial period with molossoid dogs brought to the islands, notably dogs from the British Isles in the late nineteenth century. It was used as a guard dog, a herding dog and, until dog-fighting was outlawed in Spain in 1936, for fighting.

By the 1960s the breed was close to extinction. A breed club formed in 1982, the Spanish kennel club approved its standard in 1989, and in 1991 it became a symbol of Gran Canaria. The FCI accepted it provisionally in 2001 as the Dogo Canario, definitively in 2011, and renamed it Presa Canario in 2018. Importation and sale are prohibited in Australia and New Zealand.

The Presa Canario is a large dog with a robust, muscular body and a broad, massive, square head. Where cropping is banned the ears hang close to the head in a pendant or rose shape. The upper lip is pendulous but not excessively so, and the inside of the lips is dark. The international standard revised in 2023 set lower weights than the 2018 version.

Available sources say little about temperament beyond the breed's traditional work. As a dog long kept for guarding property and controlling cattle, it is generally described as a watchful, protective working dog, and owners are commonly advised to provide early socialization and consistent training.

Sources give little specific guidance on care. As a large, powerful working breed, it is likely to need regular exercise, firm handling and enough space; prospective owners should check local rules, since some countries restrict the breed.

A study of dogs in the United Kingdom found a median longevity of 7.7 years for the breed, markedly lower than the 12.5-year median for all dogs. Sources name no specific conditions; breed clubs generally recommend health screening of breeding stock and regular veterinary check-ups.

faq.q: How big does a Presa Canario get?
faq.a: It is a large dog, roughly 56–65 cm at the withers and about 40–65 kg, with females usually smaller than males.

faq.q: How long do Presa Canarios live?
faq.a: One UK study found a median longevity of 7.7 years, well below the median for dogs overall.

faq.q: Is the Presa Canario recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI accepted it provisionally in 2001 under the name Dogo Canario, definitively in 2011, and renamed it Presa Canario in 2018.
